title: Add visual API functions to React client
description:
Modify react_ui/src/api/client.ts to add TypeScript fetch functions for all visual/image API endpoints: generate image, understand image, get image, list images, get appearance, update appearance, manage outfits.

Before editing, inspect:
- AGENTS.md
- docs/plans_tasks.md
- docs/architecture.md
- react_ui/src/api/client.ts (existing API client — understand base URL configuration, fetch wrapper patterns, TypeScript interfaces vs types, naming conventions, and error handling patterns)

Do not infer APIs, constructor signatures, function names, module locations, or service topology from the task description alone. Inspect the referenced documents and existing implementation files first, then implement against the actual repository.

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY react_ui/src/api/client.ts. Do NOT modify any other file under any circumstance. Do NOT update documentation, READMEs, operations guides, or any code outside the listed path. If you believe other files need updating, ignore that impulse and finish the task with only the listed file modified. Out-of-scope edits will cause the task to be rejected.

Implementation details:

1. Open react_ui/src/api/client.ts and inspect the existing API function patterns: base URL configuration, fetch wrapper conventions, TypeScript naming (interfaces vs types, PascalCase vs camelCase), error handling, and export style.

2. Add TypeScript interfaces/types matching the expected API shapes:
   - `ImageGenerationRequest`: scene_description (string), width? (number), height? (number), negative_prompt? (string | null), seed? (number | null).
   - `ImageGenerationResponse`: image_id (string), image_url (string), mime_type (string), seed_used (number), prompt_used (string), width (number), height (number), generation_time_ms (number).
   - `ImageUnderstandingRequest`: question? (string | null), detail_level? ('brief' | 'standard' | 'detailed').
   - `ImageUnderstandingResponse`: image_id (string), description (string), detected_objects (string[]), detected_text (string | null), scene_category (string | null), confidence (number), processing_time_ms (number).
   - `ImageView`: image_id (string), source_type ('generated' | 'uploaded' | 'understood'), image_url (string), mime_type (string), prompt_used (string | null), description (string | null), width (number | null), height (number | null), created_at (string).
   - `ImageListResponse`: images (ImageView[]), total (number).
   - `AppearanceProfile`: character_seed (number), character_description (string), visual_traits (string[]), art_style (string), color_palette (string[]), created_at (string), updated_at (string | null).
   - `AppearanceUpdateRequest`: character_description? (string), visual_traits? (string[]), art_style? (string), color_palette? (string[]).
   - `OutfitView`: outfit_id (string), name (string), description (string), visual_tags (string[]), is_active (boolean), created_at (string).
   - `OutfitCreateRequest`: name (string), description (string), visual_tags (string[]).
   - `OutfitListResponse`: outfits (OutfitView[]).

3. Add async fetch functions following the existing client.ts patterns:
   - `generateImage(sessionId: string, request: ImageGenerationRequest): Promise<ImageGenerationResponse>`: POST to `/images/generate` with session_id in body.
   - `understandImage(sessionId: string, file: File, question?: string): Promise<ImageUnderstandingResponse>`: POST to `/images/understand` with multipart form data.
   - `getImage(imageId: string): Promise<ImageView>`: GET `/images/{imageId}`.
   - `listImages(sessionId: string, offset?: number, limit?: number): Promise<ImageListResponse>`: GET `/images/` with query params.
   - `getAppearance(companionId: string): Promise<AppearanceProfile>`: GET `/images/appearance/{companionId}`.
   - `updateAppearance(companionId: string, request: AppearanceUpdateRequest): Promise<AppearanceProfile>`: PATCH `/images/appearance/{companionId}`.
   - `lockCharacterSeed(companionId: string, seed: number): Promise<AppearanceProfile>`: PUT `/images/appearance/{companionId}/seed` with seed in body.
   - `listOutfits(appearanceId: string): Promise<OutfitListResponse>`: GET `/images/outfits/{appearanceId}`.
   - `createOutfit(appearanceId: string, request: OutfitCreateRequest): Promise<OutfitView>`: POST `/images/outfits/{appearanceId}`.
   - `activateOutfit(appearanceId: string, outfitId: string): Promise<OutfitView>`: PUT `/images/outfits/{appearanceId}/{outfitId}/activate`.

4. Do NOT remove or rename existing exported functions. Do NOT change the base URL configuration or fetch wrapper pattern.
